body.statement: Uniformly over the instrumental fixed-radius subclass \(P\in\mathcal M\), the construction in \(\texttt{def:cross-fitted-primitive}\) satisfies \(\max_k\|\widehat h_k-h\|_{\infty}=O_P(n^{-\beta}\sqrt{\log n})\) for \(h\in\{p,g,m,r\}\), where \(\beta=1/2-(d+1)/(4s)>5/12\), and \(\|\widehat\theta'-\theta'\|_{\infty,J}=O_P(n^{-\beta_1}\sqrt{\log n})\), where \(\beta_1=1/2-(d+3)/(4s)>0\). These are consequences to be proved from the strengthened fixed-radius conditions, not assumptions imported from a comparator.
body.justification: This derives concrete nuisance rates on the explicitly instrumental smooth subclass before checking them against the separate Gumbel-scale remainder threshold.
body.gap: Doss (2026) formulates pointwise product-remainder conditions and Takatsu and Westling (2025) analyze different local-linear uniform remainders; neither source assumes or supplies this proposal's common global fixed-radius \(C^s\) class.
body.consumer: The displayed exponents can guide a future fully specified implementation, but are not yet a theorem about the frozen learner map.

obligation.what_is_open: A theorem for the frozen learner requires a single measurable sample map, including a chosen kernel, boundary moment equations, a density-normalization map, and a convention on singular empirical Gram matrices.
obligation.obstruction: The frozen nuisance learner denotes a family of boundary-corrected local-polynomial procedures. Different members have different boundary matrices and exceptional-sample behavior, so a probability statement about that symbol is not well typed as a claim about one estimator.
obligation.attempted: The uniform bias and stochastic terms, the derivative cost, both advertised exponents, and stability under integration and well-conditioned quotient formation were derived for every fully specified regular implementation.
obligation.partial_result:
Put \(D=d+1\).  For any completely specified boundary local-polynomial implementation with a bounded compactly supported product kernel, degree at least \(\lceil s\rceil\), uniformly nonsingular population boundary moment matrices, and a declared measurable convention on singular empirical matrices, Taylor expansion and a uniform Bernstein-net argument give, for \(j\in\{0,1\}\),
\[
 \max_{1\le k\le K}
 \left\|\partial_a^j\widehat h_k-\partial_a^j h\right\|_\infty
 =O_P\!\left(h_n^{s-j}+
       \sqrt{\frac{\log n}{n h_n^{D+2j}}}\right).
\]
Here the display applies to the \(D\)-dimensional primitives, while the \(d\)-dimensional density estimator is no slower.  At the frozen bandwidth \(h_n=n^{-1/(2s)}\), the bias is at most \(n^{-1/2+j/(2s)}\), whereas the stochastic term is
\[
 n^{-1/2+(D+2j)/(4s)}\sqrt{\log n}.
\]
Consequently
\[
 \max_k\|\widehat h_k-h\|_\infty
 =O_P\!\left(n^{-\beta}\sqrt{\log n}\right),
 \qquad
 \beta=\frac12-\frac{d+1}{4s},
\]
and
\[
 \max_k\|\partial_a\widehat m_k-partial_a m\|_\infty
 =O_P\!\left(n^{-\beta_1}\sqrt{\log n}\right),
 \qquad
 \beta_1=\frac12-\frac{d+3}{4s}.
\]
The restriction \(s>3(d+1)\) yields
\[
 \beta>\frac12-\frac1{12}=\frac5{12},
 \qquad
 \beta_1>
 \frac12-\frac{d+3}{12(d+1)}
 =\frac{5d+3}{12(d+1)}>0.
\]
By \(\texttt{ass:p-bounds}\) and \(\texttt{ass:overlap}\), denominators are bounded away from zero.  The maps used to form products and quotients are therefore locally Lipschitz on the fixed bounded range, and integration over the unit covariate cube is a contraction in supremum norm.  In particular,
\[
 \|\widehat\theta'-\theta'\|_{\infty,J}
 \le
 \|\partial_a\widehat m-\partial_a m\|_\infty
 +\|\partial_a m\|_\infty\|\widehat p-p\|_1
 =O_P\!\left(n^{-\beta_1}\sqrt{\log n}\right).
\]
This establishes the advertised exponents for every implementation satisfying the displayed implementation conditions.  It does not establish the target for the frozen symbol \(\widehat\eta\), because that symbol does not choose a kernel or boundary moment system, does not specify the density-normalization map, and has no value on a singular empirical Gram matrix; hence it is not a single measurable map of the sample.
